summary: Fourteen days of high-coverage Nightscout data show strong overall time in range with excess time below range, especially locally 23:00-03:00 and 18:00-19:00, and afternoon highs without any logged carbs. The selected AAPS profile is complete and treated as applicable. Observed meal execution is UAM-only. Competing IOB, DynISF, GLP-1, and unannounced-intake explanations are not separated, so every profile and AAPS inventory value is kept.

analysis_steps.findings: CGM coverage is 98.7 percent over 14 days with 10 gaps, largest 65 minutes, and no invalid or duplicate glucose rows. The authoritative aaps_profile is complete. Carb treatments are zero and all sampled therapy windows are correction boluses, so later CR and meal-bolus inference is limited by logging, not by a missing profile.
analysis_steps.evidence: 3995 valid entries, coverage 98.7 percent, treatments 2315, insulin 275.95 U, carb_entries 0, profile_context historical_applicability yes, empty meal_strategies array.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No activity log, no confirmed mapping of u200 dilute pump units to biologic units, and no historical profile object from before the 13 Aug switch.

analysis_steps.findings: Mean glucose 121.6 mg/dL, TIR 86.0 percent, TAR 8.9 percent, TBR 5.1 percent, CV 32.6 percent. Severe lows include 41-42 mg/dL. Local TBR clusters at 01:00 (18.5 percent) and 19:00 (15.3 percent). Afternoon TAR peaks at hour 16. This forbids adding overnight insulin or stacking more meal-time automation until lows are explained.
analysis_steps.evidence: glucose_summary, hourly_glucose_local, glucose_extremes, mixed high-TBR days such as 18 Aug, loop IOB samples up to about 5.9 U.
analysis_steps.dependencies: data_quality shows carbs are unlogged, so meal versus insulin effects remain mixed.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No hypo-treatment, exercise, or alcohol flags.

analysis_steps.findings: Overnight target 90 mg/dL with basal 0.6 U/h sits on the overnight mean and coincides with high TBR. Hours 04:00-08:00 are stable, so the 05:00-06:00 basal steps are not a dawn hole. Afternoon highs occur while basal is reduced to 0.5 U/h at 16:00, but unlogged intake and late IOB are equally or more plausible. No basal or target segment is changed.

analysis_steps.findings: CR cannot be tested with zero carb entries. Flat ISF 56 mg/dL/U is not aggressive versus TDI, while DynISF supplies much lower effective sensitivity when high. DIA 10 h can leave afternoon UAM active in the evening and overnight TBR bands. CR, ISF, and DIA are kept.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM are on, always-SMB is on, and COB-triggered SMB is off, matching cob 0. UAM is the meal path, not a second COB counter. More SMB is unsupported because afternoon highs already occur with always-on UAM and evening-night lows follow. Settings kept.

analysis_steps.findings: Autosens is off. DynISF at 70 percent is the working sensitivity layer and can explain both afternoon catch-up and later overshoot, so ISF 56 is not changed. Inventory max basal 12 U/h and max IOB 25 U exceed TDI; enacted basal is already limited near 4 U/h by multipliers. Carb-absorption settings are idle. All six AAPS groups kept.

Observed execution is correction and UAM only. Adding prebolus or a meal percent on top of always-SMB, UAM, and DynISF would raise hypo risk.

analysis_steps.findings: Ranked causes: unannounced or delayed intake plus UAM and DynISF explain 09:00-17:00 highs better than weak 16:00 basal or weak ISF 56. Late UAM or DynISF IOB plus DIA 10 h and target 90 explain 18:00-19:00 and 23:00-03:00 lows better than a proven overnight basal excess. Conflicts are unresolved enough that no inventory item changes. Safe order is keep profile, observe nights and log meals, then consider one later automation-limit review, never pairing SMB delivery with DynISF, ISF, or afternoon basal.

analysis_steps.data_gaps: Need IOB at overnight hypo onset and 3-5 logged eating events.

strengths: CGM coverage 98.7 percent is adequate for pattern review.
Overall TIR 86.0 percent with modest TAR.
Local 04:00-08:00 is highly stable, which argues against increasing early-morning basal.
The selected profile is complete and internally UAM-first, matching zero COB.
The loop already sets zero temps when predicted guard glucose is low.
issues: TBR 5.1 percent with severe lows to 41-42 mg/dL.
Recurring local 18:00-19:00 crash after afternoon peaks.
Afternoon TAR without any carb announcements.
High glucose variability (CV 32.6 percent) and days that mix high TAR with high TBR.
Meal strategy is undeclared and unlogged, so CR and bolus timing cannot be tested.
Max IOB 25 U and max basal 12 U/h are far above observed TDI, even though multipliers already cap enacted basal near 4 U/h.

recommendations.title: Keep overnight basal and target and verify IOB at lows first
recommendations.description: Local 23:00-03:00 TBR is the strongest safety pattern, but leftover UAM or DynISF IOB, DIA 10 h, target 90 mg/dL, and basal 0.6 U/h are not separated. Raising overnight insulin is unsupported. Cutting basal or raising target now would mix those causes.

suggested_change.first_action: For several nights record glucose and IOB at the start of any low between local 23:00 and 03:00.

recommendations.title: Log meals before any afternoon CR, basal, or SMB review
recommendations.description: 09:00-17:00 highs and the 16:00 CR 10.5 g/U and basal 0.5 U/h segments remain confounded by zero carb entries and UAM. Meal logging changes the safe order by blocking those dependent changes.

suggested_change.first_action: Record clock time, carb grams or an explicit unlogged-on-purpose note, and whether any insulin was given before the first bite for 3-5 typical eating events.

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Keep every current basal, target, CR, ISF, and DIA value. First verify local 23:00-03:00 lows against IOB and unlogged evening intake instead of changing a profile number.
profile_recommendation.rationale: Overnight means sit near the 90 mg/dL target with high TBR, but afternoon UAM, DynISF, and DIA 10 h can supply that insulin. Hours 04:00-08:00 are already stable. Daytime CR and ISF have no clean meal or correction experiments. Package evidence therefore supports keeping the profile while one observation separates leftover IOB from basal.
profile_recommendation.next_check: On the next 5 nights, note IOB and recent SMB or UAM when local glucose first falls below 70 mg/dL between 23:00 and 03:00.

parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: local 23:00-03:00 TBR 10-18 percent with little TAR. Uncertainty: leftover evening UAM or DynISF IOB and DIA 10 h are competing causes. Dependencies: do not cut this basal in the same step as target, SMB, or DynISF.
Evidence: local 04:00-06:00 TIR 95-97 percent with almost no TAR. Uncertainty: one isolated 42 mg/dL near 06:19 on 21 Aug. Dependencies: overnight TBR review comes first.

Evidence: local 06:00-08:00 remains high TIR and is not a dawn-high pattern. Uncertainty: single early low should not drive an increase. Dependencies: safety_overview forbids adding morning insulin to treat one extreme.
Evidence: late-morning rise is meal-clock shaped after the 08:00 target change. Uncertainty: unlogged intake versus basal. Dependencies: meal logging before any daytime basal change.

Evidence: hour 16 has the highest TAR, but 18:00-19:00 TBR follows the same insulin. Uncertainty: unlogged meals, GLP-1 delay, and UAM lag. Dependencies: CR 16:00, SMB or UAM, and DIA must stay unchanged in the same step.
Evidence: local 18:00 already has 7.7 percent TBR after the afternoon peak. Uncertainty: residual IOB versus this basal step. Dependencies: evening hypo brake from safety_overview.

Evidence: local 19:00 TBR 15.3 percent with minima 41 mg/dL. Uncertainty: delayed afternoon insulin rather than this 0.7 U/h step. Dependencies: do not raise this segment while 18:00-19:00 lows persist.
Evidence: zero carb entries, so this ratio was unused. Uncertainty: cannot estimate meal response. Dependencies: meal announcement data.
Evidence: no overnight or dawn carb treatments. Uncertainty: segment may be unused. Dependencies: carb logging.
Evidence: morning rise occurred with cob 0, so UAM not CR delivered insulin. Uncertainty: unlogged breakfast versus CR. Dependencies: meal_bolus_strategy.

Evidence: strongest CR coincides with peak TAR and later TBR, but no carbs were logged. Uncertainty: UAM substitution versus an unused strong CR. Dependencies: do not change with 16:00 basal or SMB delivery.
Evidence: evening windows are correction or UAM only. Uncertainty: no meal-linked CR test. Dependencies: evening hypo risk and DIA.

Evidence: static 56 is not aggressive for TDI about 20 U, while variable_sens often ran 28-54 when high. Uncertainty: corrections are mixed with SMB, DynISF, site issues, and unlogged carbs. Dependencies: keep DynISF unchanged in the same step.
Evidence: overnight means hug 90 mg/dL while TBR is high. Uncertainty: leftover IOB may be the driver, so a target change is not yet isolated. Dependencies: basal 00:00 and evening automation.

Evidence: daytime target 100 mg/dL sits below afternoon means that look meal-driven. Uncertainty: tightening it would add UAM exposure into the evening crash. Dependencies: SMB always-on and hypo brake.
Evidence: local 23:00 already has about 10 percent TBR. Uncertainty: same leftover-IOB versus target question as 00:00. Dependencies: keep with overnight basal; do not tighten.

Evidence: long DIA can connect afternoon UAM to 18:00-03:00 lows. Uncertainty: insulin peak is not given and dilution is unconfirmed, so shortening DIA is unsupported. Dependencies: ISF, SMB, and overnight basal interpretation.

Evidence: this pair matches zero COB and is the observed meal path. Uncertainty: UAM likely contributes to late lows, but turning it off would be a second meal algorithm without carb data. Dependencies: activation and delivery groups.

Evidence: always-SMB with COB SMB off is consistent with cob 0 and high-TT SMB already off. Uncertainty: always-SMB may over-deliver on unannounced rises, but disabling it is not isolated from DynISF. Dependencies: meal logging before any activation change.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS max basal U/h and max IOB U
parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: ceilings exceed TDI about 20 U and sampled IOB about 5.9 U; enacted basal already near 4 U/h. Uncertainty: lowering them would not have changed most of this curve and needs a later single-item review. Dependencies: profile and SMB or DynISF stay first; do not bundle a limit change with insulin-profile edits.

Evidence: DynISF 70 percent already varies effective ISF widely and can create both afternoon catch-up and later lows. Uncertainty: enabling Autosens would add a second sensitivity layer. Dependencies: keep profile ISF and SMB delivery unchanged in the same step.
Evidence: both values were idle with zero COB. Uncertainty: no meal-linked absorption to test. Dependencies: e-carb and CR review require carb entries first.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Keep the executed plan as UAM-only with no prebolus, no announced immediate bolus percent, and no e-carbs until meals are logged and evening or overnight lows are reviewed.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: User-declared meal_strategies is an empty list, so no prebolus minutes, bolus percent, or e-carb fields exist. Telemetry shows 0 g carbs and correction or UAM insulin only. Adding a prebolus or e-carbs on top of always-on SMB, UAM, DynISF, and DIA 10 h would stack insulin into the known 18:00-03:00 TBR bands.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: For 3-5 typical eating events, record time, carb grams or an explicit unlogged-on-purpose note, and whether any insulin was given before the first bite.

exceptions.pattern: Large local 12:00-17:00 rise, sometimes on GLP-1 note days, then 18:00-19:00 crash.
exceptions.suggestion: If a meal in that window is later announced, do not add an early full prebolus on top of current UAM and DynISF; announce first and watch 4-6 hours.
exceptions.rationale: The delayed peak plus long DIA is the strongest TAR-to-TBR flip and is not a second fully specified meal recipe.

implementation_steps: Leave all current profile and AAPS inventory values in place for this review cycle.
Independently confirm the selected profile, u200 dilute context, and that no other change is made at the same time.
For about 5 nights, mark IOB and recent SMB or UAM when local glucose first falls below 70 mg/dL between 23:00 and 03:00.
In parallel, log 3-5 eating events with time, grams or explicit unlogged intent, and any pre-bite insulin.
Only if nights still go low with little leftover IOB, discuss one overnight item later, either basal 00:00 or target 90 mg/dL, not both.
Only after meal logs exist, consider a later single review of oversized max IOB or max basal, without changing SMB minutes or DynISF in that same step.
Do not change 16:00 basal, 16:00 CR, ISF 56, DynISF 70 percent, and SMB delivery together.
Monitor glucose closely after any future single change and revert that one change if lows increase.
education: Time below range clustered after afternoon highs often means insulin arrived late, not that the afternoon basal number is proven too low.
UAM doses unannounced rises and is not the same as counting those rises as COB.
A sensitivity_ratio of 1 is a neutral current adjustment and does not mean Autosens is enabled; Autosens is off in this profile.
DynISF can make effective ISF much stronger than the profile 56 mg/dL/U when glucose is high, then leave IOB for many hours when DIA is 10 h.
E-carbs are a carb-absorption announcement, not a pump extended bolus, and none were present here.
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only and is not medical advice.
The user must independently verify every proposed change with their care team.
Make at most one change at a time and monitor glucose closely.
Do not increase overnight insulin or add prebolus, e-carbs, or stronger SMB while 41-42 mg/dL lows and evening or overnight TBR continue.
Treat occlusion, site-change, sensor-change, and GLP-1 days as confounders rather than clean profile tests.
